idiom_name: immutable record State + record Action hierarchy + Reduce switch expression + event/IObservable state stream
implementation_notes: No MVI framework is standard on .NET, so the loop is hand-written: records carry the state and the action hierarchy, a pure Reduce(State, Action) with a switch expression (C# 8+ patterns) decides the next state, and a state holder publishes it through an event, IObservable (System.Reactive) or a callback list while Blazor/MAUI/WPF views bind to the published state. Fluxor supplies a Redux-style store with reducers and effects for Blazor when an app-wide store is genuinely wanted, but the intent-reduce-state loop itself is written by the team, and the dominant .NET UI pattern remains MVVM (CommunityToolkit.Mvvm). Hand-writing is justified when one-way transitions, replay and state restoration matter more than the boilerplate; a small MVVM view model with INotifyPropertyChanged is the simpler alternative.
pitfalls: A record is only shallowly immutable: a List<T> inside the state still mutates the published snapshot; expose ImmutableArray or copies.
Publishing state from a background thread while WPF/MAUI binds on the UI thread throws or corrupts binding state; marshal notifications to the dispatcher.
Subscribing to the state event with += and never unsubscribing keeps views alive and updates dead controls; unsubscribe on teardown or use weak subscriptions.
A new action type falls into the discard arm of the switch expression silently; keep the default arm explicit and log unknown intents.
